items.title: Share these readings with your care team
items.text: You had an average sugar level of 181.9 mg/dL, which is higher than the target. Bring this to your next visit to discuss with your team.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal went with a smaller rise in sugar, about 3.2 to 18.3 mg/dL smaller. Try walking after meals, but ask your care team about it if you take insulin or certain medications.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: 58.3% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later. Across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones in the same person, and 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a quarter of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Eating dinner late, at 8 pm or later, went with a higher rise in sugar, about 9.2 mg/dL more. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it helps.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 12.1 hours of overnight fasting, which is a good habit to keep. Fasting overnight may be linked to sugar, and you had 25.0% of nights with 13 hours of fasting.
